title: How to build a product catalog image standardization workflow at scale
summary: Learn how to implement product catalog image standardization with Photoroom. Build a repeatable workflow for marketplace-ready images at scale.
body_text: A product image that fails a marketplace’s background, size, or format rules can get rejected, which means the listing can’t go live until you correct the image. That becomes a serious production problem at scale . For example, preparing 1,000 SKUs for five sales channels creates about 5,000 image outputs, and editing that manually (which takes about 15 minutes each ) adds up to more than 15 weeks for two designers. Successful product catalog image standardization turns those repeated fixes into an automated workflow for each category and channel. Once you set the specifications, you can apply them to new images, update folder assets in batches, and produce consistent listing visuals without rebuilding every file by hand. Table of contents: Where product catalog management often fails How to build a repeatable product catalog image standardization workflow: 6 steps Standardize your e‑commerce images at scale with Photoroom Frequently asked questions Where product catalog management often fails Even if you have a process that works for managing a hundred e‑commerce products, that doesn’t guarantee consistent results as your catalog grows . The problem usually isn’t the standards themselves, but how you approach day-to-day production. Every new product introduces another opportunity for exceptions, manual decisions, and duplicate work. Over time, those exceptions become part of the workflow, making it harder to apply the same specifications across every image. Here are some of the most common points where your product catalog may start to lose consistency. Image reviews become production bottlenecks Reviewing product images before publication helps you catch issues early, but as more SKUs move through production, review queues can grow to unmanageable sizes. This leaves teams to respond in one of two ways: delaying launches until images are approved, or shortening reviews to keep products moving. Neither approach solves the underlying production problem. It’s more likely that either your launch timelines will slip, or images will reach production without meeting your standards. Different teams create inconsistent assets Marketing, marketplace operations , regional teams, and external agencies may all create or update versions of the same asset for different purposes. Without a shared production workflow, those versions tend to gradually drift apart. Finding the latest approved asset becomes another manual task that consumes resources. Teams have to spend time comparing files and replacing outdated images, as well as correcting the inconsistencies that spread across sales channels. Manual edits are difficult to reproduce reliably Two editors following the same style guide can interpret positioning and cropping guidelines differently, especially when they’re working on images weeks or months apart. Those variations may accumulate across your catalog and require expensive refreshes or rebranding projects to fix. Marketplace requirements multiply production work Each marketplace has its own image specifications, like preferred aspect ratios and background requirements. Some teams respond by exporting separate image versions for every channel, instead of applying those specs through a repeatable workflow. This approach creates duplicate assets that increase the likelihood of outdated files and failed marketplace submissions. Managing e‑commerce catalog updates creates ongoing rework New channels, updated marketplace requirements, seasonal campaigns, and packaging changes typically introduce new rounds of image updates. Without a repeatable production workflow, your team will have to treat each change as an additional editing project. Instead of updating one standard and applying it across the catalog, your team needs to revisit thousands of existing assets individually. The result is more reworks, slower product launches, and less time for new catalog initiatives. How to build a repeatable product catalog image standardization workflow: 6 steps Consistent brand image standards define what every product photo should look like before it reaches your catalog. These standards specify details like subject positioning, dimensions, file formats, and any category-specific treatments your products require. But those specifications are more valuable and achievable when treated as production rules instead of reference documents. That’s why Photoroom helps you build an automated e‑commerce asset workflow , letting you apply image specifications across your catalog at batch scale. Here’s how you can use Photoroom’s AI image creation and editing tools to standardize and produce studio-quality, marketplace-ready visuals. 1. Define your category image standards Start by documenting the visual requirements for each product category. Define background colors, framing, padding, aspect ratios, and output dimensions. With Photoroom, you can save these standards as custom templates . You only need to create a template once for a particular category or channel, then you can apply it to new catalogs and collections indefinitely. And you can keep all categories looking consistent by using Brand Kit to add in elements like preferred logos and fonts. 2. Standardize outputs for every sales channel You’ll also need to consider the formatting and styles each marketplace requires or prefers. For example, main images on Amazon must have pure white backgrounds, while Etsy photos tend to convert best when they show products in realistic contexts. Features like Image Resizer and Background Generator help you prepare channel-specific outputs. You don’t need to maintain separate editing workflows for every destination, and you can still keep each sales channel aligned with the same production standards. 3. Audit and organize your image library Before applying new standards, review your existing catalog. Look for duplicate assets, inconsistent crops, outdated product photos, and images that no longer meet your current criteria or branding. Then group visuals that need updates into batches based on the changes required. That way, you can quickly apply the same edits in bulk, instead of treating every product as a separate editing project. 4. Apply e‑commerce edits at scale Now that your images are organized, you can use Photoroom’s Batch mode to make changes and apply templates. Photoroom’s Pro, Max, and Ultra plans let you apply AI editing features, such as Background Remover , AI Shadows , Retouch , and Background Generator, to up to 250 images at once. Batch mode will make identical edits across all those photos, keeping your catalog visually aligned without sacrificing product details or image quality. If you’re working with larger catalogs, Photoroom’s Enterprise API lets you build production pipelines that quickly process thousands of SKUs. 5. Apply category-specific visual treatments Some categories require special treatment to produce product images that convert. For instance, apparel catalogs benefit from features like Ghost Mannequin and AI Fashion Models , which let you show how clothes look when worn. For furniture and home goods, you can use Product Staging to display them in lifelike contexts. And you can update product variations without extra shoots using tools like Recolor Clothing and Product Beautifier . These tools all benefit from AI trained on e‑commerce best practices, and they work within the same batch image editing workflow we looked at earlier. This lets you optimize and standardize entire collections, each one full of realistic, studio-quality product images that are ready for listing. 6. Validate and publish your images Review each completed batch to confirm that it matches your brand and category standards. Then you can export images in bulk for upload to your storefront or marketplaces. Depending on your plan, you can export between 500 and 10,000 listing-ready visuals per month. If you sell on Shopify, you can publish listing visuals straight from the Photoroom interface. Standardize your e‑commerce images at scale with Photoroom Product catalog image standardization is the result of a consistent production system, not repeated manual efforts. Organizations that systematize e‑commerce visuals early don’t have to recreate the same editing process each time they launch new product lines or expand into more marketplaces. Photoroom helps you build that production system, with AI/automated product photography tools that apply consistent, studio-quality edits at scale. Features like Brand Kit and custom templates let you set catalog-level and category-specific specs, then apply them to all your listings using Batch mode .

Available through August 30, the Fuzzy's Beach Club menu is built around the fresh flavors and nostalgic California coastal vibes that made the sun-soaked summer days of yesterday memorable: delicious food, cold drinks and good company, no plane ticket or beach pass required. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260707323606/en/ Fuzzy's Taco Shop Serves Up an Endless Summer with a New Beach Club Menu & Exclusive Offerings The Fuzzy's Beach Club menu brings together the greatest hits of summer nostalgia, where beach-town staples, boardwalk favorites and Fuzzy's-style twists show up everywhere from beer-battered fish and loaded fries to a cocktail built for savoring every sip of summer: Cali-Style Steak Taco ($5.35): Grilled steak and crispy seasoned fries piled onto a flour tortilla with house-made guacamole, pico, diced pickled jalapeños and chipotle aioli. Baja Fish Taco ($4.55): Fuzzy’s signature fish taco, now featuring a Pacifico beer-battered fish served on a soft corn tortilla with shredded cabbage, cilantro-lime crema, pickled onions, signature Fuzzy Dust, cilantro and a fresh lime wedge. title: Klarna to power Apple Upgrade, a new hardware leasing program offered by Apple | Klarna International
body_text: New York, July 28, 2026 - Klarna, the global digital bank and flexible payments provider, today announced it would be the leasing provider behind the Apple Upgrade program, a new hardware leasing option available from Apple in the United States. Lease Apple hardware for low monthly payments Provided by Klarna, Apple Upgrade offers customers a new way to pay for eligible iPhone, Mac, iPad and Apple Watch. Customers can select from 12- and 24-month leasing options for iPhone and Apple Watch, and 24- and 36-month leasing options for Mac and iPad. In addition, when customers first enroll in Apple Upgrade, they can trade in an existing device to further lower their monthly payments during their initial lease term. The freedom to upgrade, return, or buy When the lease ends, customers choose what suits them: upgrade to the latest model*, purchase their device, or return it. A seamless checkout, and easy to manage payments Apple and Klarna have built an easy and seamless checkout experience which shows customers exactly what customers are agreeing to before they enter into a lease. Upon choosing their preferred device and leasing term customers can apply at Apple Retail, both online, in-store, and Apple Store app. Customers can apply within minutes, and if approved by Klarna, can complete their transaction at Apple Retail and Apple Store as usual. In-store customers can enjoy their new device right away, while online customers can choose delivery or in-store pickup. Customers can see their upcoming payments in the Klarna app and stay on top of their lease from start to finish. The Klarna leasing option is available now on the Apple Store online, in the Apple Store app, and at Apple Store locations in the United States. *Upgrades require entering into a new lease and returning your prior device, and are subject to eligibility and credit approval.

title: Media statement: Solvinity acquisition decision
summary: Kyndryl responds to the Netherlands’ decision on Solvinity and reaffirms its commitment to customers, security and innovation.
body_text: We are extremely disappointed by the Netherlands’ government decision to prohibit Kyndryl’s acquisition of Solvinity. Since announcing the proposed transaction, Kyndryl has consistently engaged in good faith with relevant stakeholders across the Netherlands’ government. Despite this engagement and our long history of managing mission-critical operations in the Netherlands, the politicization of this process has overshadowed the clear and important benefits this transaction would have brought to Solvinity’s customers and Dutch citizens. Notwithstanding this outcome, our team will continue to support our customers in the Netherlands as they modernize legacy systems, keep pace with rapid advances in technology and do so securely and at scale. We will continue to bring our proprietary agentic AI methodologies to regulated and non-regulated customers across the Netherlands. Our team will, as they always have, operate with trust and dedication to the highest standards of mission-critical services, security, compliance, data protection and innovation. We are grateful to our Kyndryl Netherlands employees. They have exemplified professionalism and commitment to our customers and each other throughout this process. About Kyndryl Kyndryl (NYSE: KD) is a leading provider of mission-critical enterprise technology services, offering advisory, implementation and managed service capabilities to thousands of customers in more than 60 countries. As the world’s largest IT infrastructure services provider, the company designs, builds, manages and modernizes the complex information systems that the world depends on every day. For more information, visit www.kyndryl.com . Kyndryl press contact press@kyndryl.com

title: Celebrating Kennametal’s Legacy in Turning
summary: Celebrate Kennametal's long history in turning and discover why they have become a leader in manufacturing. Plus, learn about some of the newest innovations.
body_text: With deep expertise in developing cutting-edge coatings and grades for turning solutions, Kennametal continually sets the standard for innovation and new technology. It all began in 1972 with the launch of our KC75 physical vapor deposition (PVD) grade, followed by the KC710 chemical vapor deposition (CVD) grade in 1985 – achievements that paved the way for more advancements. As our PVD and CVD technologies evolved, they culminated in the creation of KENGold,™ a premium coating solution available in both PVD and CVD processes and engineered to meet the demands of next-generation machining. The legacy continues with KCP25C , a standout CVD grade featuring an advanced MT-TiCN/Alumina CVD coating. It’s designed for durability and precision, and helps reduce waste by making it easier to spot worn or unused edges when machining carbon, alloy and various other steels. Complementing everything is our high-performance KCU10B and KCU25B PVD grades. Both deliver outstanding resistance to thermal deformation edge wear across all material groups. KCU10B is the harder, more wear-resistant option, while KCU25B is tougher, catering to different machining needs. These grades excel in machining steels, stainless steels, cast iron and high-temp alloys . “Turning grades are the backbone of precision machining,” says Etling. “Each new generation improves on the last, ensuring every cut is precise, every edge is resilient, and every operation is efficient. These grades aren’t just materials—they’re engineered solutions that deliver superior performance and durability.”

title: How a rambuncous horse is helping improve ADT security systems
summary: When Trashy the horse escaped his pen, it was a chance for an ADT engineer to test the value of his security system.
body_text: Alex Crettenand was sitting in his office, more than an hour from home, when he received a notification on his ADT+ app that an animal was in his driveway. Not a squirrel or even a raccoon. It was a horse. A quick check of Crettenand's live Google Nest camera feed revealed the details: one of his horses, Trashy, had escaped his pen and was happily wandering the property, grazing on the front lawn and enjoying his newfound freedom. Crettenand, ADT's VP of Software Engineering, has outfitted his working horse ranch in Texas with the company's second-largest ADT+ Security System deployment, boasting 18 security cameras, 26 sensors, 8 connected Z-Wave devices, two thermostats and more. It’s a fun and convenient way to keep tabs on his ranch and the often-amusing antics of the four horses his wife, Victoria, trains. But, above all, it’s a real-world testing ground for ADT+ software. Check out the video to see Trashy's antics. A true security test case The alert about Trashy the horse wasn’t random. Google Nest cameras, as part of the ADT+ smart home ecosystem, are designed to distinguish between people, vehicles and animals, sending notifications based on what matters most to the user. In this case, customized activity settings flagged movement on the driveway, helping Crettenand know fast that something out of the ordinary was occurring. Back at home, Trashy had made himself comfortable, nibbling on fresh grass and rolling in the yard. It was funny to watch him frolic, Crettenand said, but it also provided meaningful reassurance that his system was helping him keep watch at home. And it helped keep Trashy safe. After seeing that the horse was loose, Alex was able to contact a neighbor who got the horse safely back into his pen. That’s what smart protection is all about: helping you stay connected to home, wherever you are. From a package delivery to an unexpected visitor — or a horse with his own plans — you can see what’s happening and respond quickly when it matters most. Start configuring your smart security system at ADT.com . About the author Brad Dash ADT Communications Manager #Google #Innovation #Smart home

title: Huntington Bank Commits $80 Billion to Support Affordable Housing, Small Businesses and Local Communities
summary: The new Community Plan will expand access to capital and strengthen financial well-being across Huntington's markets. COLUMBUS, Ohio, July…...
body_text: The new Community Plan will expand access to capital and strengthen financial well-being across Huntington's markets. COLUMBUS, Ohio , July 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Huntington Bancshares Incorporated (Nasdaq: HBAN) today announced a new $80 billion Community Plan. The plan will help improve financial opportunities for consumers, businesses and communities with a focus on affordable housing, small business and community development investments. Huntington shaped the plan by listening first. Company leaders met with more than 350 community organizations, including members of the National Community Reinvestment Coalition (NCRC), along with customers and colleagues, to identify the areas of greatest need. "For 160 years, Huntington has invested in the people, businesses and communities we serve. That commitment doesn't change as we grow — it deepens," said Steve Steinour, Huntington chairman, president and CEO. "This plan reflects the way we've always worked: listening to the communities we serve, showing up consistently and putting our resources where they can do the most good." "This plan means more mortgages for first-time homebuyers, more capital for small businesses trying to grow and more investment in the neighborhoods that need it," said Brant Standridge, president of Consumer and Regional Banking. "It's the kind of work Huntington has been doing for generations — and the work our teams in every market are committed to continuing." The five-year plan focuses on four areas: Consumer and Home Lending — $40 billion: Mortgage and consumer lending to help more customers purchase homes and access affordable credit, including first-time homebuyer programs. Small Business — $22 billion: Lending to support small business formation, growth and job creation. Community Development Lending and Investing — $18 billion: Larger-scale loans and investments that finance affordable housing developments, small business lending programs, and community services such as food security, financial empowerment and workforce development. Under-Resourced Communities — $32 billion of the total $80 billion plan: Capital directed to communities with greater economic need. "When financial institutions make bold commitments and invest in strong community partnerships, the impact extends far beyond dollars and cents," said Jesse Van Tol, CEO of the National Community Reinvestment Coalition (NCRC). "Small businesses grow, neighborhoods become more vibrant and families gain access to opportunities. Huntington's Community Plan demonstrates how intentional investment can help drive meaningful outcomes." This plan builds on Huntington's prior Community plans and has delivered nearly 270,000 loans totaling $37.8 billion to low-and moderate-income borrowers, small businesses, and under-resourced communities, along with more than $12.3 billion in community development lending and investments since 2021. About Huntington Huntington Bancshares Incorporated is a $284 billion asset regional bank holding company headquartered in Columbus, Ohio. A top 10 U.S. commercial bank, the Huntington National Bank and its affiliates provide consumers, small and middle-market businesses, corporations, municipalities, and other organizations with a comprehensive suite of banking, payments, wealth management, and risk management products and services. Founded in in 1866, Huntington operates over 1,400 branches in 21 states, with certain businesses operating nationally. Visit Huntington.com for more information.
